name: AT24C32
full_name: Atmel/Microchip AT24C32 32Kbit (4K x 8) I2C Two-Wire Serial EEPROM
description: The AT24C32 is a 32 Kbit (4,096 x 8) two-wire serial EEPROM operating from 1.8V to 5.5V with 100/400 kHz bus speeds and a 32-byte page write buffer. It belongs to the same 8-pin I2C family as the larger 24Cxx devices and uses three address pins for up to eight devices per bus. Endurance is one million write cycles with 100 years retention. Its standout trait is being the EEPROM chip soldered onto nearly every cheap DS3231/DS1307 RTC breakout module, sitting at I2C address 0x57 alongside the clock.

pins.name: WP
pins.description: write protect; high disables writes, low/floating enables them

typical_application: On-board nonvolatile scratch storage on DS3231/DS1307 RTC modules and small config storage.
gotchas: on DS3231/DS1307 modules it appears at 0x57 by default (A0-A2 pulled high); cut traces or repull to relocate it
page size is 32 bytes, half that of the 24LC256, so existing page-write code must use the smaller boundary
needs SDA/SCL pull-ups; on RTC modules these are usually already populated, so do not stack more low values
WP pad is often tied low on modules; if you want write protection you must access that pin
write cycle is up to 10 ms, longer than the larger parts; use ACK polling and do not assume 5 ms
do not confuse with the AT24C32 vs AT24C32N/D revisions which differ slightly in voltage/timing specs
